data.cultural_impact: The name Waheebah holds significant cultural value as it signifies being a giver, both materially and spiritually. In many Muslim communities, charitable giving or Zakat is an essential practice, and the name could serve as a constant reminder to be generous and selfless. Furthermore, the given name could also mean that the child is expected to be a blessing or source of joy to their family and community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Waheebah carries a profound meaning as it represents the concept of being a giver, as explained in numerous Hadiths and Islamic teachings. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) once said, "The best house is the house in which the name of Allah is mentioned most frequently, and the best family is the one in which Prophet Muhammad is most remembered," signifying that giving and being generous, in words, actions, or spirit, brings immense blessings. Living a life that reflects the name Waheebah, where one gives unconditionally and carries out good deeds, would lead to a great reward in the hereafter.

historical_references.context: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami was a prominent Islamic scholar and jurist, and his work is considered a significant source for the study of Islamic history and jurisprudence.
